title: 244 years ago today: the violinist who 'sold his soul to the devil' | Paganini

lines: Legend says he sold his soul to the devil.

Two hundred and forty-four years ago today, in Genoa, Italy,

lines: His father traded at the harbor, and played the mandolin.
His father ran a small trade at the harbor, and in his spare time, played the mandolin.
Niccolò picked up the violin at seven,
Nikolo picked up the violin at seven,
and before twelve, gave his first concert in a church.
and before he turned twelve, he gave his first public concert in a church.
At eighteen, he became first violinist of the Republic of Lucca.
In 1807, for Napoleon's name day,
In eighteen-oh-seven, for Napoleon's name day,
he wrote a violin sonata
played entirely on a single string.
Others used four strings. He used one, and stunned the crowd.
Everyone else used four strings. He needed just one, and the audience was stunned.
From 1828, he toured across Europe,
From eighteen twenty-eight, he toured across Europe,
and conquered Vienna, Paris and London.
His fingers moved impossibly fast, and audiences gasped.
Some people even swore they saw the devil helping him play.
A young pianist named Franz Liszt was spellbound,
and vowed to become the Paganini of the piano.
His twenty-four Caprices
are still the ultimate test for violinists around the world today.
He died in Nice in 1840.
He died in Nice in eighteen forty.
He left his violin, the Cannon, to Genoa,
He left his favorite violin, the Cannon, to his hometown of Genoa,
where winners of the Paganini Competition still play it.
They called him the devil,
but his technique made the violin limitless.
but what he really left behind was a technique that made the violin limitless.
His question for you: if you had only one string left,
what would you play?
